newsitem.title: USA: Elizabeth Taylor "up and about" in hospital.
newsitem.headline: Elizabeth Taylor "up and about" in hospital.

text.p: Actress Elizabeth Taylor spent the day resting in the hospital on Sunday from a mild seizure that put her back there three days after being discharged following surgery to remove a benign tumour.
The Oscar-winning screen star, who was re-admitted on Saturday to Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre, was in good condition and "up and about," hospital spokesman Ron Wise said on Sunday afternoon.
But he said she was still awaiting word on when she could go home and by 4 p.m. PST (7 p.m. EST) (0000 GMT Monday) it was unlikely she would be discharged on Sunday, he said.
"She's very alert and whatever it was has passed completely and there's been no recurrence," Wise said earlier in the day. "I would hope for a short stay," said Wise.
Shirene Coburn, Taylor's publicist, said on Saturday that the actress had suffered a mild seizure at home but stressed such seizures are a common side effect of brain surgery.
"She's up and alert, she's fine," Coburn said. "She's undergoing routine tests."
However, Coburn was not available on Sunday for an update on when Taylor might be discharged from the Beverly Hills hospital.
Taylor underwent four hours of surgery on Feb. 20 to remove an apparently benign tumour the size of a golf ball from the lining of her brain.
Taylor celebrated her 65th birthday on Thursday, one day after she was released from the hospital.
